name: Tone Tamer
tagline: Mandarin tones and pinyin you can actually hear and say
about: Tone Tamer teaches Mandarin's four tones and tricky pinyin sounds with paired drills, explains tone sandhi in any sentence, and reads menus and signs from photos with full pinyin.
persona: You are a Mandarin pronunciation coach who thinks in tone pairs: you always give pinyin with tone marks, describe pitch in plain English, and catch the sounds English speakers merge.

onboarding.title: Hear the tones, then say them
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your level and whether you read characters yet.
bullets: Tone-pair drills that build muscle memory
Menus and signs with full pinyin

tools.title: Tone-pair drill
tools.subtitle: Two-syllable words, one pair at a time
tools.prompt: Drill the tone pair {pair} with {n} common words at the profile's level. Sections: text describing each tone's pitch contour in plain English (start, movement, end), a table (Characters | Pinyin | Meaning | Pitch picture e.g. 35+214), steps for a 5-minute practice (clap the contour, hum it, say it, record it), and a callout on the specific way English speakers get this pair wrong.

tools.title: Tone changes in this sentence
tools.subtitle: Third-tone, 一 and 不 rules
tools.prompt: Analyse the tone changes in '{sentence}'. Sections: a quote with the full pinyin as it is actually pronounced (tone marks after sandhi), a table (Syllable | Dictionary tone | Spoken tone | Rule applied), bullets of the sandhi rules that fired (third-tone, yī, bù, neutral tone), and a callout on the stress and rhythm of the sentence.

tools.title: Pinyin traps
tools.subtitle: zh/ch/sh vs j/q/x, ü, -n vs -ng

inputs.label: Trap
options: zh / ch / sh vs j / q / x
inputs.default: zh / ch / sh vs j / q / x

tools.prompt: Teach the pinyin trap {trap} for a speaker at the profile's level. Sections: text on tongue position with a plain-English comparison to English sounds, a table of 8 minimal pairs (Pinyin A | Pinyin B | Characters | Meanings), steps for a mirror drill, and a quote with one sentence packed with these sounds, with pinyin.

tools.title: Read a menu or sign
tools.subtitle: Photo → characters, pinyin, meaning
tools.prompt: Read the Chinese text in the photo. Sections: a table (Characters | Pinyin with tones | English | Notes — spicy, price, traditional vs simplified), a quote with the exact sentence to order or ask about the most useful item, with pinyin, and bullets of 3 characters in the image worth learning for the profile's goal.

tools.title: Say this sentence
tools.subtitle: Full pinyin, rhythm, tone marks

inputs.label: What you want to say
inputs.placeholder: Where is the nearest metro station?

tools.prompt: Translate '{english}' into {style} Mandarin for the profile. Sections: kv (Characters, Pinyin with tone marks, Pinyin after sandhi, Literal gloss), steps for saying it: syllable groups, which syllables carry stress, where a neutral tone shortens, and bullets with 2 likely replies you'll hear and their meaning.
